pillar_reactions.evidence: Arrived already converted and self-serving the pillar: bought a Bowflex adjustable kettlebell a month before the call, started following Trevor's YouTube workouts, and reported results in a week — 'I could visibly see in just a week with regards to how my body actually changed, with just few workouts that I did 25-30 minutes a day... without any proper nutrition plan.' He tied the modality to his own affect: 'I feel fun when I do it. I feel like my body reacts good.' He also connected the mobility component to his own back pain unprompted and validated it from experience: 'when I did this kettlebell thing for about a week, week and a half, I just felt like my glutes and my low back actually started working better.' On the morning mobility routine he answered 'I started doing that actually last year.'

The only pillar he interrogated, and he asked about mechanics rather than pushing back: 'so how will the nutrition plan sort of work? Is it more of like, hey, here are the list of foods that you can potentially eat, and does it also give guidance on, let's say I'm breaking my fast at 2 p.m., what's the best thing that you can eat at this time?' The fasting alignment is his primary purchase driver and he said so explicitly: 'it's very tough to find a coach who also believes in this whole fasting thing, because for me, it's very, very important. And people that I've spoken to, when I say this, they are like, oh no, you'll have to eat something in the morning.' The rep matched it with Trevor's monthly full-moon fast, which the prospect had already seen on video. His vegetarian protein constraint was acknowledged and deferred to the coach rather than answered.

The pillar he most needed and recognised as such: 'I feel great with regards to this. I feel like this is what I need, this constant person to keep pushing you, motivating you, and just giving you honest, like these knocks, right? Like, hey, you didn't do it today, like what happened?' The video form-check landed hardest because it named the exact failure of his last coach: 'I feel like this is what I lacked when I did the personal trainer one, because that person was not here, and there was no mechanism for me to actually know if I'm doing the things right or not... I had to ask someone at the gym, hey, is my form right? And that made me question, why do I even need a personal trainer.' He then extended the mechanic himself: 'it also builds a bit of accountability, right? Because I need to actually make effort to actually put in.'

anchors.raw: I didn't know that it was going to be a 6k investment. So yeah, I was like, I was thinking more so of like 2k or like, like three. So that's what I was thinking. I didn't think it was going to be a bit more stretch.
anchors.note: He had pre-discussed a number with his wife before the call and it was less than half the actual price, which is why the reaction was audible surprise — 'That's quite a lot. Wow. I did not expect this.' The anchor was formed before the call and shared with the decision-making household, so the rep was negotiating against two people's expectations, not one. Worth tracking upstream: a setter or an application flow that let a prospect arrive expecting $2,000-$3,000 created this.

anchors.raw: for the past one month, honestly, I've actually invested in a kettlebell, like in my house, I actually got Bowflex... and then I started watching some YouTube videos of Trevor, and then I started making some things, and I could visibly see in just a week with regards to how my body actually changed
anchors.note: The same pattern as the Chris call on 3 July: the prospect is already getting results from the coach's free content with his own equipment. It cuts both ways here — the free trial is what convinced him the modality works and drove the application — but nothing in the presentation quantified what $6,000 adds over what he is already doing successfully for nothing. The rep never asked what he thought was missing beyond the prospect's own volunteered answer of guidance and form feedback.

anchors.raw: he'll just give me like a big plan of, hey, go to the gym and do X, Y, and Z workouts, and then just come. I don't know if my form is right, and I had to ask someone at the gym, hey, is my form right? And that made me question, like, why do I even need a personal trainer if I have to ask someone at the gym?
anchors.note: A burned buyer whose specific grievance is exactly what the offer's video form-check solves. The rep used it well by letting the prospect make the connection himself. He never asked what that trainer cost, which would have given the only real price reference on the call.

anchors.raw: my son is also starting school, and that's about 24K a year. So that's where the majority of the money goes into.
anchors.note: Alongside remittances to his parents in India and his wife launching a small business with earmarked funds — 'few other things that we had in our mind to sort of do in the next two, three months, we need to figure out how we are going to reposition it.' The constraint is allocation rather than capacity, which is why an instalment structure rather than a discount was the correct response and worked.

anchors.raw: I do have good limits. I have maybe in total 60, 70k limits.
anchors.note: Surfaced only because the rep ran the full open wallet. It is the single fact that made the deal viable and it would not have existed on a call run the way the Tom or Chris calls were run. Note the rep did not then push the card — he offered it as one of two options and let the prospect pick instalments from surplus instead.

anchors.raw: since you have credit cards and a good limit, we can actually don't use the savings and put it on a credit card and use the, do you know Klarna? Yep. Yeah. So we're not using Klarna, we are using Pava financing. And that's, you can split up to even 12 months.
anchors.note: Second appearance of the Pava financing product in this batch. Here it was offered as an alternative rather than a rescue, and the prospect declined it in favour of paying from surplus. No interest rate or total cost of credit was stated on either call it appears on.

unmet_demand.want: Results by 1 December, five months from the call, as a birthday gift to his son
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is a six-month transformation and a 4 July start lands in early January. The rep did not correct the date; he endorsed it twice — 'we're having, like, July, August, September, October, November. That actually fits in' and 'to get you to that version 2.0 of Hari, as we spoke, for the first December 1st, the investment is 6K.' The prospect's whole emotional case is built on that date.

unmet_demand.want: Protein programming for a vegetarian who eats in a four-hour window and cannot cook eggs at home
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep acknowledged the constraint and deferred — 'we have vegetarians and vegans on the board, but it needs some adjustment... Trevor will be working with you on dialing in the nutrition.' Nobody established that this has been solved before for a combination of vegetarian, at-home egg restriction and 18-20 hour fasts, which is materially harder than any of those alone.

unmet_demand.want: A coach who programmes around 18-20 hour daily fasting rather than prescribing six to eight meals a day
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Substantially served — this is the reason he applied, and the rep matched it with Trevor's own fasting practice. It is listed here because it was answered by affinity rather than by evidence: no example was given of a client programmed on a 20:4 window, and it is the prospect's stated deal-breaker.

unmet_demand.want: Confirmation that the adjustable kettlebell he already bought is adequate — 'I've invested in a kettlebell, which may not actually be the best one'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Raised twice by the prospect and never answered by either side. Equipment requirements were not discussed at any point, and a Bowflex adjustable behaves differently from a cast bell in ballistic work. Small, but it is an unresolved cost and safety question that a buyer is entitled to have answered before paying.
